title: Ordinary derived immersion and representable-chart comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $T$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the constant ring sheaves $C_{n,T}=(R/t^n)_T$, and $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}C_{n,T}$ with projections $\pi_{T,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For a scheme morphism $g:T\to W$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $g^{-1}$ and $c^g_{R/t^n}$ be the inverse image and constant-section maps [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Give it the structural ring map $c_g:g^{-1}B_W\to B_T$ characterized by $\pi_{T,n}c_g=c^g_{R/t^n}g^{-1}(\pi_{W,n})$. Write $g_B^*M=B_T\otimes_{g^{-1}B_W}g^{-1}M$ for ordinary module pullback, and $P_g=Lg_B^*$ with computation counit $\epsilon_Q:P_g[Q]\to[g_B^*Q]$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Here module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $[Q]$ denotes localization, and tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes, let $i:S\hookrightarrow Y$ be a locally closed immersion (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion) [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion], and put $X_S=X\times_Y S$, $j:X_S\hookrightarrow X$, $f_S:X_S\to S$. Let $u:U\to S$ be an object of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and put $V=X_S\times_S U$, $v:V\to U$. For every $K\in D(B_Y)$ there are natural isomorphisms
$$j^*P_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{f_S}(i^*K),\qquad
(j^*P_fK)|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}P_v((i^*K)|_U).$$
Here $i^*,j^*$ are ordinary exact immersion restrictions [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison], and $r_U=(-)|_U$ and $r_V=(-)|_V$ are exact restrictions to the localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], identified with the sites of $U,V$ with their completed coefficient rings and finite projections. The first isomorphism is the composite of the ordinary derived composition comparisons for $fj=if_S$ and the canonical two-isomorphism transport of their structural ring maps. For the second, the canonical isomorphism $f_S^{-1}h_U\cong h_V$, where $h_U=\operatorname{Hom}_S(-,U)$ and $h_V=\operatorname{Hom}_{X_S}(-,V)$, identifies the element-site ringed slice morphism $(f_S)_{h_U}$ with the ringed morphism $v$ and its map $c_v$. The second comparison is the restriction of the first followed by the inverse of the canonical derived slice comparison $P_{(f_S)_{h_U}}r_U\cong r_VP_{f_S}$. Both isomorphisms use the ordinary K-flat representative comparisons, before completion. There is no noetherianity, completeness, boundedness, separatedness, base-field, or structural-map flatness hypothesis.

proof.text: Ordinary completed-coefficient pullback preserves finite limits by lem-tw-ordinary-completed-pullback-exact, while its specified adjunction gives finite colimits. Use the exact functor mapDerivedCategory for every Image. Its factorization isomorphism supplies the counit, the universal left-derived property follows by localization, and its counit is invertible on all complexes, hence on the specified Good complexes.

proof.text: Take the adjuncts of completedRingMap_comp. Their composition equation makes the sectionwise module pushforward compositors linear. Compose the compositor for c,d, the sectionwise pushforward comparison across a;b=c;d (constructed from the site eqToIso with pushforwardCongr₂, avoiding whole-functor transport), and the inverse compositor for a,b. Its section map is precisely squareSiteIso by the presheaf map-comp equation. Take its unique adjunction mate to construct the ordinary Square. Apply the exact-derived square comparison. Its factorization equations give ImmersionSquare.normalization on every complex by cancellation, so no separate K-flat resolution argument is needed.

proof.text: Use lem-tw-ordinary-completed-chart-comparison for the underived represented chart square with its specified section map and adjunction mate. Chart restriction preserves finite limits and finite colimits: the Over.map functor is continuous and cocontinuous, and forgetting modules identifies its pushforward with abelian restriction. The exact-derived square comparison then gives Chart.comparison. The same exact-derived factorization calculation gives Chart.normalization on every complex.

proof.text: Restrict the immersion comparison by the derived exact restriction rV, reassociate, whisker the inverse chart comparison by Pi, and reassociate back. This defines Comparison.comparison with Comparison.formula by reflexivity.

lean.statement: theorem ordinaryImmersionChartComparison {X Y S : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : S ⟶ Y) [IsImmersion i] (U : S.ProEt) : Nonempty (Comparison l E f i U)
lean.note: The main theorem asserts existence of the normalized Comparison record. Its Image fields are universal ordinary derived pullbacks with their computation counits; ImmersionSquare and Chart retain the two natural isomorphisms, actual structural maps, sectionwise direct-image comparisons, adjunction-mate normalizations and K-flat representative equations. Comparison.formula fixes the second isomorphism as restriction of the first followed by the inverse slice comparison. All module and coefficient constructions are existing APIs; no completeness or finiteness hypothesis on schemes or complexes is added. Scheme and coefficient universes remain independent.

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause check of node vs Lean: IsImmersion = closed then open; X_S/j/f_S = pullback/fst/snd; V = proEtaleBaseChange f_S U; v = completedRingSliceArrow; c_g = completedRingMap (choice from the unique-existence statement with the node's projection equations); pull = Mathlib ordinary sheafified pullback; Image = IsLeftDerivedFunctor + K-flat computation. First iso fixed by normalization against square.ordinary, which is the adjunction mate of a sectionwise direct map via squareSiteIso (fibre-product compositors + eqToIso of pullback.condition). Second iso = Comparison.formula, restriction of the first then inverse Chart.comparison; types checked. Both normalizations determine the isos (counits invertible on good complexes), so no free arrows. Linearity comes from completedRingMap_equal_composites and the completedRingMap_slice c_v clause. chartRingIso choice is fixed by its constants and projection clauses. No extra hypotheses; edge cases i=id, f=id, U=S, empty schemes, zero/unbounded complexes; universes t,u independent. Only the lean field changed; statement verbatim; 21/21 declarations; docstrings with source, blueprint and 4 proof steps; no line over 100 chars; only the theorem is sorry.
